_comment: Per-Article native-unit manifest for build/build-standalone.sh. Only Articles with native-Typst units need UNITS; any article with an empty units list (4-9) renders as pure markdown in a single pandoc pass. Per unit: typ (native file under source/), splice (after-prose | at-marker:<NAME>), data (--input data= value), conditional_on (path under source/ that must exist or the unit is skipped), parity (pad-to-odd-before = pad a blank so the unit's first page lands on a verso, e.g. Art-2 D1), pad_to (even-block = pad a trailing blank to keep an even block; only relevant mid-document, a no-op when the unit is last).
_ownership_comment: data_sources declares which files carry an Article's binding content, for the substantive-change determination. Each entry is {path, compare}: json-keyed (keyed leaf diff; carries key, and substantive_fields when only SOME fields are substantive -- when substantive_fields is ABSENT every leaf is substantive), binary-hash (report 'changed (binary)' and require a recorded human call), or generated-from (carries from; counts only through that file, and a change with an unchanged source is an ANOMALY). The FORM of key is interpreted by the consumer, not defined here: it mixes a path mini-grammar ('[].code', 'segments[].id') with a '$'-prefixed sentinel, and each entry's _key_note says what it means -- defining the grammar is the consuming tool's job. A path ending in / claims every tracked file beneath it. PRECEDENCE AND EXACTLY-ONCE: every tracked file under source/ must have exactly one claimant (build/tests/test_manifest_ownership.py fails otherwise, naming the file). The top-level shared and ignored lists are TERMINAL -- a path listed in either is claimed by that list alone, even if it also falls under a / prefix, which is how a file inside a claimed directory is carved out. Two Articles claiming the same path is a test failure, not a tie-break. PROSE IS NOT DECLARED HERE: ownership of an Article's prose is the article-0N-*.md convention, which is also build-standalone.sh's fallback, and declaring it would change manifest.py prose's output for Articles 4-9. OPEN -- what a change to a file in shared implies for the substantive-change determination is NOT decided. The candidate rule is that it flags every Article for a standalone and a standalone redline (standing rule 4), but nothing relies on it and shared is currently empty; the operator rules before the first entry is added. INTERIM (Ben Frey, 2026-10-09): build/czc_diff.py REFUSES, naming the file, when a changed file is listed in shared, until a person decides which Articles it affects. What IS settled: shared is a claimant of last resort, not an exemption -- a path goes there only when no single Article owns it. manifest.py data <NN> LISTS NON-PROSE FILES ONLY: prose is claimed by the article-0N-*.md convention and is never in data_sources, so data 7 returns [] although Article 7's binding content is entirely its prose -- an empty data_sources list never means no binding content.
_md_completeness_note: md_completeness declares what a standalone .md holds: complete (all of the Article), prose-only (its text; native pages are named by pointer notes), prose-plus-appendix (its text plus a generated appendix of its native pages). build/czc_md.py refuses a declaration that contradicts the Article's units.
_ignored_note: legacy/article-02-districts.md is the retired markdown form of the district tables (Article 2 is native Typst now). inventory-sample.json is the LIVE Typst default for both Article 3 exhibit units (street-type-inventory.typ:23 and street-type-map.typ:40 read sys.inputs.at('data', default: 'exhibits/street-types/inventory-sample.json')); it is ignorable ONLY because this manifest always supplies the real data: path, so it never reaches a build -- if a unit stopped being given data:, the sample would silently become what the Code prints. sprites/NOTICE.md is a license notice for the sprite artwork, not a standard; it is carved out of the sprites/ prefix below because the lists are terminal.

data_sources._note: scanned/raster map exhibits: a pixel diff cannot say whether a boundary moved, so report 'changed (binary)' and require a recorded human call

units.label: the thirteen district pages (district standards and use tables)

data_sources._key_note: the file is a bare LIST of 13 district objects, keyed by code AND name: code alone is not unique -- seven districts are 'SD', and a code-only key would merge them
data_sources._excluded_note: group, color and band_text are presentation: they change what the spread looks like, not what is permitted

data_sources._key_note: an object keyed by Type code (S1..R5) plus a _meta block; no substantive_fields, because every field of a Type entry is printed Code -- code, footnote, family, name, context, description, purpose, note, row, edges, segments, standards, applies_in, attributes (14 fields)
